newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran oil minister predicts higher budget surplus.
newsitem.headline: Iran oil minister predicts higher budget surplus.

text.p: Iranian Oil Minister Gholamreza Aghazadeh said in remarks published on Sunday that he expected Iran to post a higher budget surplus this year and that any oil price changes would not negatively affect state earnings.
"In 1995 we had a surplus of $1.6 billion and in 1996 the surplus was 3.5 billion," he told Sunday's edition of the English-language daily Kayhan International.

"This success was achieved due to the preventive measures taken by the government and Majlis (parliament) during the past years. The surplus in the budget this year is expected to be higher than the previous years," he added.
Aghazadeh said "any new changes in the (oil) market will not have a negative impact on our earnings".
Oil is Iran's largest single earner, contributing some 40 percent to state budgeted revenue. Iran has based its March 1997-1998 budget on an oil price of around $17.50 a barrel.

In January Iran's parliament approved a 188.6 trillion rial state budget for the Iranian year starting on March 21, 1997. Iran regularly predicts a balance between state income and spending in its budget, but some deputies had predicted a 25 percent deficit, saying revenues would fall short of forecast.

The dollar value of the budget could range from $107.8 billion, if calculated at the official exchange rate used for essential state accounts -- 1,750 rials to the dollar -- down to $62.9 billion at Iran's other official rate -- 3,000 rials to the dollar -- which the government appears to use increasingly.
